title: Reading a Whole Sentence: Ready for Intro
overview:
No new spellings. You have them all.
Six words that break every rule.
Then a whole sentence, left to right.
Then the Intro level.
functions: Read the words that phonics cannot read
Find where a sentence starts and ends
Read a whole sentence from left to right
Read a sentence out loud, without stopping
Write a sentence with a capital and a full stop
Say what you can do now and what comes next
learningPath: Words: six hard ones, and the words for reading.
Patterns: the hard words, sentences, going on.
Read a sentence out loud. Record it.
Practice and quiz. Check your answers.
lectureScript:
This is Unit 20. The last one.
There are no new spellings today.
You have every one of them.
Two things left. Then you are done.
The first is a short list of words.
These break every rule you have learned.
You cannot sound them out. Nobody can.
Would. Could. Two. Four. Because. People.
Look at would. W, o, u, l, d.
The l says nothing at all.
Look at two. T, w, o.
The w says nothing either.
People. That should be pee-oh-ple.
It is not. It is pee-pl.
There are about a hundred words like this.
A hundred, out of many thousands.
You learn them by sight, the way you did the.
And you meet them every single day.
So they come quickly.
Now the second thing. A whole sentence.
Until now you read words. One at a time.
A sentence is words in a line, with a job.
It starts with a capital letter.
It ends with a full stop.
Those two marks tell you where to start.
And where to stop and take a breath.
Read left to right. Always left to right.
Do not look ahead. Do not jump back.
If a word stops you, say its sounds.
Then go on. Do not start the line again.
Read the whole sentence. Then read it once more.
The second time is always better.
That is the last thing this level teaches.
And now you are ready for the Intro level.
Intro does not teach reading. It teaches English.
Your name. Your job. The time. A shop.
It asks you to read, and now you can.
Twenty units. Well done. Go on.

grammar.title: The words phonics cannot read
grammar.explanation:
Some words break every rule.
You cannot work them out. Nobody can.
There are about a hundred, and you meet them daily.
grammar.rule:
would   the l says nothing
could   the l says nothing
two     the w says nothing
four    not like for
because not like cause
people  said pee-pl
grammar.workedExample:
You meet the word people.
1. Try the sounds first. Always.
2. Pee-oh-ple. That is not a word.
3. So it is one of the hundred.
4. Look at it. Say it. Look away. Say it.
5. Three times a day for three days.
grammar.mistake:
Grinding at a word that cannot be decoded.
Try the sounds once. If it fails, learn it whole.
grammar.tip: A hundred words. Thousands follow the rules.
grammar.practice:
Read these by sight.
1. would
2. could
3. two
4. four
5. because
6. people
grammar.answers:
There is no working out here.
Check: each one read without stopping?
Not yet? Look, say, look away, say.

grammar.title: Where a sentence starts and ends
grammar.explanation:
A sentence is words in a line, saying one thing.
Two marks tell you where it begins and ends.
Find them before you read.
grammar.rule:
The bus was late.
^                ^
capital          full stop

A capital letter starts it.
A full stop ends it.
That is where you breathe.
grammar.workedExample:
You see a long line of words.
1. Find the first capital letter.
2. That is where the sentence starts.
3. Now look for the next full stop.
4. That is where it ends.
5. Read from one to the other. Then breathe.
grammar.mistake:
Reading past a full stop runs two ideas together.
Stop at the dot. Take a breath.
grammar.tip: Capital to full stop. Then breathe.
grammar.practice:
How many sentences? Count the full stops.
1. I got up. I went to work.
2. The bus was late.
3. It was cold. I had no coat. I ran.
4. She said no.
5. We ate. Then we went home.
6. Well done.
grammar.answers:
1. two
2. one
3. three
4. one
5. two
6. one
Five or six right? You can see a sentence.

grammar.title: Reading a whole sentence
grammar.explanation:
Until now you read one word at a time.
Now you read a line of them, in order.
Left to right. Never back.
grammar.rule:
1. Start at the capital.
2. Read each word, left to right.
3. A word stops you? Say its sounds.
4. Then go ON. Do not start again.
5. Stop at the full stop.
6. Now read the whole thing once more.
grammar.workedExample:
You read: The people were late because of the bus.
1. Capital T. Start there.
2. The. People. Were. Late.
3. Because stops you. Say it by sight.
4. Go on. Of. The. Bus.
5. Full stop. Breathe. Read it again.
grammar.mistake:
Going back to the start after every hard word.
You never reach the end that way. Go on.
grammar.tip: One hard word does not cost the sentence.
grammar.practice:
Read each sentence twice. Was the second better?
1. I would like a cup of tea.
2. Two people were late.
3. I could not read it because it was dark.
4. Four of us went home.
grammar.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: did you read left to right each time?
Did you go on after a hard word?
Was the second reading better than the first?

grammar.title: What the Intro level asks of you
grammar.explanation:
This level taught you to read the letters.
The next one teaches English.
It asks you to read, and now you can.
grammar.rule:
Phonics    the sounds, the spellings, the words
Intro      your name, your job, the time, a shop

Intro has 16 units.
It reads at about the level you are now.
It will not ask you to sound out a word.
grammar.workedExample:
You are about to start Intro.
1. You can read a short sentence.
2. You can sound out a word you do not know.
3. You know the hundred hard words are hard.
4. That is everything Intro needs.
5. Keep a word list. Read it out loud daily.
grammar.mistake:
Stopping here because it feels unfinished.
Reading gets better by being used, not by more phonics.
grammar.tip: Read every day. Ten minutes beats an hour.
grammar.practice:
Say these out loud, about yourself.
1. I can read a sentence.
2. I am ready for the next level.
3. The next level is Intro.
4. Well done.
grammar.answers:
There is no key. These are yours to say.
Check: did you say all four out loud?
Did you mean them? You should.

readings.title: The First Day
readings.genre: Whole sentences, with capitals and full stops
readings.setting: A first morning at a new job
readings.passage:
I would not say it was fun.
Two people came with me.
We were late because the bus did not stop.
The man at the gate had four names on a list.
He said: you are late, but go in.
I could read the list.
That was new, and it felt good.

readings.title: Everything You Can Read Now
readings.passage:
would could two four because people
phone white wheel city cent age page giant
turn saw more house boy care near work
home slow toe June blue new note few
eat dream time night my try five light
name late day pay make take away game
car fork bird her cow coin hear hair
wait feet pie boat boot foot rain week
sing bank thin this shop chin cash much
stop trip clap swim drum flag desk jump

That is over two hundred words.
In Unit 2 you could read four.

readings.title: You Are Ready
readings.setting: The wall card, the last one
readings.passage:
You finished the Phonics level.
Twenty units. Well done.

The next level is Intro.
It teaches English, not reading.
It will not ask you to sound out a word.

Read something out loud every day.
Ten minutes beats one long hour.

comprehension.q: How many people came with the writer?

comprehension.why: The word because gives the reason.

comprehension.q: What did the man at the gate say?
comprehension.a: You are late, but go in.

comprehension.q: Count the full stops. How many sentences?
Read line three out loud. Did you go on?
comprehension.a: Any honest answer. Because is a hard word.
comprehension.why: Going on is the skill, not getting it first time.

comprehension.q: How many words could you read in Unit 2?
comprehension.why: The last line of the list says it.

comprehension.q: Read one row out loud. Which was hardest?
comprehension.a: Any honest answer. Name the row.
comprehension.why: Naming the hard row tells you what to read again.

comprehension.q: What does the next level teach?
How long should you read each day?
comprehension.why: The last line of the notice.

comprehension.q: Read the whole notice out loud, twice.

speaking.title: Speaking 1 — The six hard words
speaking.instructions:
Read these by sight. Do not sound them out.
would
could
two
four
because
people
Look. Say. Look away. Say again.
Tap the mic. Read them all.
Check: did you read each one without stopping?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to use because in a sentence.

speaking.title: Speaking 2 — A whole sentence
speaking.instructions:
Read each sentence. Left to right. Do not go back.
I would like a cup of tea.
Two people were late.
Four of us went home.
Tap the mic. Read all three.
Check: did you get to the full stop each time?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor to listen for where you stopped.

speaking.title: Speaking 3 — Twice is better
speaking.instructions:
Read this sentence twice.
I could not read it because it was dark.
Slowly the first time. Better the second.
Tap the mic. Read it twice.
Check: was the second one better than the first?
speaking.tutor: Ask the tutor which of your two readings was better.

speaking.title: Speaking 4 — Say it, then write it
speaking.instructions:
Say a sentence about today. Then write it.
Start with a capital. End with a full stop.
Do that three times.
Tap the mic. Say all three.
Check: did each one start and end right?
speaking.tutor: Read your three sentences to the tutor.

speaking.title: Speaking 5 — Read the list, faster
speaking.instructions:
Read the first row of the word list twice.
would could two four because people
The second time, try not to stop.
Tap the mic. Read the row twice.
Check: was the second time easier?
speaking.tutor: Read the row to the tutor. Ask which words were not clear.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — What you can do now
speaking.instructions:
Say these out loud, about yourself.
I can read a sentence.
I am ready for the next level.
The next level is Intro.
Tap the mic. Say all three.
Check: did you say them and mean them?
speaking.tutor: Tell the tutor one thing you can do now that you could not.

writing.title: Writing 1 — Four sentences
writing.prompt:
Write four sentences about your day.
A capital at the start. A full stop at the end.
writing.model: I got up at six. I went to work.
writing.criteria:
Four sentences.
A capital letter starting each one.
A full stop ending each one.
writing.extension: Now use because in one of them.

writing.title: Writing 2 — Use the hard words
writing.prompt:
Write three sentences.
Use would, because and people, one in each.
writing.model:
I would like a job.
I am late because the bus did not come.
The people at work are kind.
writing.criteria:
Three sentences.
One hard word in each.
A capital and a full stop on every one.
writing.support: Write one sentence only, with because.
writing.extension: Now use could and four as well.

activities.title: Practice 1 — The hard words
activities.instructions:
Read these by sight.
1. would
2. could
3. two
4. four
5. because
6. people
activities.answers:
There is no working out here.
Check: each one read without stopping?
Not yet? Look, say, look away, say. Three times a day.
activities.solo: Read them out loud, then check.

activities.title: Practice 2 — How many sentences?
activities.instructions:
Count the full stops. Write the number.
1. I got up. I went to work.
2. The bus was late.
3. It was cold. I had no coat. I ran.
4. She said no.
5. We ate. Then we went home.
6. Well done.
activities.answers:
1. two
2. one
3. three
4. one
5. two
6. one
Five or more right: you can see a sentence.
Below five: count the dots, not the lines.

activities.title: Practice 3 — Read it through
activities.instructions:
Read each sentence. Do not go back to the start.
1. I would like a cup of tea.
2. Two people were late.
3. I could not read it because it was dark.
4. Four of us went home.
activities.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: did you read left to right each time?
Did you go on after a hard word?
Going on is the skill here.
activities.solo: Read all four, then check yourself.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Twice
activities.instructions:
Read each sentence twice, out loud.
1. The people at work are kind.
2. I was late because of the bus.
3. Would you say that again?
activities.answers:
There is no written key.
Check: was the second reading better every time?
It nearly always is. That is why we read twice.
activities.solo: Record both readings, then listen back.

activities.title: Practice 5 — Write four
activities.instructions:
Write four sentences about today.
Capital at the start. Full stop at the end.
activities.answers:
There is no key. These are your sentences.
Check: four capitals and four full stops?
Read each one back out loud. Does it say one thing?
activities.solo: Write them, then read them back.

activities.title: Practice 6 — What comes next
activities.instructions:
Answer these out loud, then write them.
1. What can you read now?
2. What could you read in Unit 2?
3. What is the next level?
4. Are you ready?
activities.answers:
1. Over two hundred words, and sentences.
2. Four words.
3. Intro.
4. Yes.
Look at answers one and two together.
That is twenty units of work.
activities.solo: Say each answer, then write it.

quizzes.q: The word two has a letter that says nothing. It is the ___.
Words like would and people are ___.
quizzes.why: They break the rules, so you learn them whole.

quizzes.q: About how many English words break the rules like this?
quizzes.why: A hundred, out of many thousands. The rest follow the sounds.
The capital shows you where to start.

quizzes.q: How many sentences? It was cold. I had no coat. I ran.
quizzes.why: Count the full stops. One dot, one sentence.
Always the same way. Never back.

quizzes.q: A hard word stops you in the middle. You should ___.
options: say its sounds and go on
quizzes.a: say its sounds and go on
quizzes.why: Going back to the start means never reaching the end.

quizzes.q: The full stop tells you to ___.
quizzes.why: It is the end of one idea.

options: The first time does not count
quizzes.why: It nearly always is. That is the whole point.

quizzes.q: Every sentence you write needs a capital and a ___.
quizzes.why: One at each end. That is what marks a sentence.

quizzes.q: The next level after Phonics is ___.
quizzes.why: Sixteen units, and it teaches English rather than reading.

quizzes.q: How long should you read out loud each day?
quizzes.why: Ten minutes every day beats one long hour.

teacherNotes.note: Every pattern card has a worked example, every practice has a key, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back, check.

teacherNotes.type: The hard words come last for a reason
teacherNotes.note: would, could, two, four, because and people are among the commonest words in English and none of them can be decoded. Meeting them in Unit 2 would have taught a beginner that phonics does not work. Meeting them now, after two hundred decoded words, teaches that English has a short list of exceptions. Say the number: about a hundred, out of many thousands.

teacherNotes.type: Going on after a hard word is the whole skill
teacherNotes.note: The commonest failure at this point is not misreading a word; it is going back to the start of the line after every one. The learner then reads the first four words ten times and never reaches the end. Say it plainly and watch for it. One hard word does not cost the sentence.

teacherNotes.type: The second reading is where fluency comes from
teacherNotes.note: Re-reading the same sentence is not a remedial move, it is the move. 1SLp.01 is exactly this: re-read sentences aloud with some fluency. A learner who reads everything once and moves on stays slow for years.

teacherNotes.type: Do not hold a learner here
teacherNotes.note: Reading improves by being used, not by more phonics. A learner who can decode a short sentence and knows the hard words are hard has everything Intro needs. If they feel unfinished, that is normal and is not a reason to repeat units — Intro reads at about this level and never asks them to sound out a word.

teacherNotes.type: Say well done, and say what changed
teacherNotes.note: Twenty units is a great deal of work for an adult who could not read at the start. The word list in this unit is the evidence: four words in Unit 2, over two hundred now. Put the two numbers side by side out loud. It is the most motivating thing in the level and it costs ten seconds.

selfAssessment.statement: I can read would, could, two and because.
I can find where a sentence starts and ends.
I can read a whole sentence.
I can read a sentence out loud.
I can write a sentence with a capital.
I can say what I can do now.

assignment.title: Read a sentence, and write four
assignment.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Record yourself. Read the six hard words.
would, could, two, four, because, people
Then read these two sentences, twice each:
I could not read it because it was dark.
Two people were late for work today.
2. Write four sentences about your day.
A capital at the start. A full stop at the end.
Use because in one of them.
Listen back before you finish.
assignment.submissionType: Audio recording and a written page
